facts.statement: Arcticodactylus lived during the Late Triassic in what is now Greenland.
facts.quote: Arcticodactylus is a genus of basal pterosaur living during the Late Triassic in the area of present-day Greenland.

facts.statement: William Amaral discovered the fossil site of Arcticodactylus in 1989 on McKnight Bjerg in eastern Greenland.
facts.quote: In 1989, William Amaral on the McKnight Bjerg in the east of Greenland discovered a rich fossil site.

facts.statement: Farish Jenkins and colleagues named the species Eudimorphodon cromptonellus in 2001.
facts.quote: In 2001, Farish Jenkins, Neil Shubin, Stephen Gatesy and Kevin Padian named and described it as a new species of Eudimorphodon: Eudimorphodon cromptonellus.

facts.statement: The species name cromptonellus honors Professor Alfred Walter Crompton.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Professor Alfred Walter Crompton.

facts.statement: Alexander Kellner established the separate genus Arcticodactylus in 2015.
facts.quote: In 2015, Kellner named a separate genus Arcticodactylus.

facts.statement: Arcticodactylus holds the record for the smallest known pterosaur, with an estimated wingspan of 24 cm.
facts.quote: The holotype individual of Arcticodactylus is the smallest pterosaur known, with an estimated wingspan of just 24 cm.

facts.statement: Arcticodactylus possessed eleven or twelve multi-cusped teeth on each side of its jaw.
facts.quote: The jaws have eleven or twelve multi-cusped teeth per side.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Matthew G. Baron grouped Arcticodactylus within the clade Caviramidae alongside Carniadactylus and Raeticodactylus.
facts.quote: In 2020 however, a study upheld by Matthew G. Baron about early pterosaur interrelationships found Arcticodactylus to group with Carniadactylus, Raeticodactylus, and the Austriadraconidae, which in turn were within a clade he called Caviramidae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Arcticodactylus is closely related to Eudimorphodon, as researchers have noted it lacks key traits like fang-like teeth and striated enamel found in Eudimorphodon.
facts.quote: In 2014, Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia noted that E. cromptonellus shared not a single trait with Eudimorphodon ranzii not present in other pterosaurs but lacked the distinguishing fang-like teeth, pterygoid teeth and striated tooth enamel.

facts.statement: The lower jaw possessed eleven or twelve multicuspulate teeth on each side.
facts.quote: La mandíbula tiene once o doce dientes multicúspides de cada lado.

facts.statement: The femur was only slightly shorter than the tibia, measuring 96% of its length.
facts.quote: El fémur es apenas un poco más corto que la tibia, con el 96% de su longitud.

facts.statement: The scapula was much longer than the coracoid, measuring 93% of its length.
facts.quote: La escápula es mucho más larga, 93%, que el coracoides.

facts.statement: The humerus was slightly shorter than the femur at 92% of its length, and also 91% of the ulna's length.
facts.quote: El húmero es algo más corto que el fémur, con un 92% de su largo, o que el cúbito y aunque tiene el 91% de su largo.

facts.statement: The femur was slightly longer than the first wing finger phalanx, which measured 91% of the femoral length.
facts.quote: El fémur es algo más alargado que la primera falange del dedo del ala, que tiene el 91% de la longitud femoral.

facts.statement: The third metatarsal of the foot was elongated, measuring 56% of the tibia's length.
facts.quote: El tercer metatarsiano del pie es alargado, con el 56% de la longitud de la tibia.

facts.statement: These proportions imply that Arcticodactylus had relatively short wings and large feet.
facts.quote: Estas proporciones implican que Arcticodactylus tenía alas relativamente cortas y grandes pies.

facts.statement: Arcticodactylus can be distinguished from Eudimorphodon by the lack of canine-like teeth in the middle of the tooth row, and from Eudimorphodon ranzii, Carniadactylus, and Bergamodactylus by having a triangular deltopectoral crest on the humerus instead of a rectangular one.
facts.quote: Arcticodactylus puede ser distinguido adicionalmente de Eudimorphodon por la ya mencionada carencia de dientes parecidos a colmillos en la mitad de la fila de dientes y de Eudimorphodon ranzii, Carniadactylus y Bergamodactylus por una cresta deltopectoral triangular en el húmero, en lugar de ser rectangular.

facts.statement: A 2001 histological study of its bone structure suggested the holotype had not yet completed its growth but was not a newborn.
facts.quote: En una investigación de corte histológico de su estructura ósea, publicada en 2001, se consideró que aún no había completado su crecimiento, pero tampoco era un recién nacido.

facts.statement: Jenkins and colleagues proposed that the unique joint in Arcticodactylus between the main wing metacarpal and the finger represented a transitional form between ancestors with a single rounded articular surface allowing considerable lateral movement and the condition of late pterosaurs showing a slight depression or trochlea.
facts.quote: Jenkins y colaboradores afirmaron que la articulación única en Arcticodactylus entre el principal metacarpio del ala y el dedo de la misma, era una forma transicional entre sus ancestros que portaban una única superficie de articulación redondeada en el metacarpiano permitiendo un considerable rango de movimiento lateral, y l condición de los pterosaurios tardíos que muestran una leve depresión o tróclea.

facts.statement: In 2001, E. cromptonellus was placed in the family Eudimorphodontidae.
facts.quote: En 2001, E. cromptonellus fue situado en la familia Eudimorphodontidae.

facts.statement: In 2015, Kellner indicated a basal position within Pterosauria and suggested a close affinity to Austriadraco within a family Austriadraconidae based on the short coracoid.
facts.quote: Kellner en 2015 indicó una posición basal dentro de los Pterosauria, y el breve coracoides sugiere una afinidad cercana a Austriadraco dentro de una familia Austriadraconidae.

facts.statement: Arcticodactylus lived during the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Arcticodactylus belongs to the parent group Pterosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Pterosauria

facts.statement: Arcticodactylus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Arcticodactylus is Arcticodactylus cromptonellus.
facts.quote: Type species: Arcticodactylus cromptonellus
